claim: The ein6-1 mutant originates from a genetic screen of fast neutron-mutagenized A. thaliana Landsberg erecta (Ler) seeds.
source: The ein6-1 mutant originates from a genetic screen of fast neutron-mutagenized A. thaliana Landsberg erecta (Ler) seeds (Roman et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Roman et al., 1995.

claim: SHOREmap and segregation analyses identified mutations in two different genes in the ein6-1 mutant.
source: Surprisingly, SHOREmap (Schneeberger et al., 2009) and segregation analyses identified mutations in two different genes in the ein6-1 mutant (Figure 1A; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to SHOREmap methodology and references to figures showing the analysis results.

claim: Only one of the two single mutants displays an ET-hyposensitive root phenotype which is referred to as the ein6-1 single mutant.
source: Interestingly, only one of the two single mutants displays an ET-hyposensitive root phenotype which we refer to as the ein6-1 single mutant (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A showing the phenotype.

claim: The second gene mutation was named EIN6 ENHANCER (EEN) because while een-1 plants show no phenotype, ein6-1 een-1 double mutants show an ET-insensitive root phenotype.
source: The second gene mutation was named EIN6 ENHANCER (EEN) because while een-1 plants show no phenotype, ein6-1 een-1 double mutants show an ET-insensitive root phenotype (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A showing the phenotypic differences.

claim: The causal mutation at the ein6-1 allele is a seven base pair (bp) deletion in the fifth exon of the RELATIVE OF EARLY FLOWERING6 (REF6, At3g48430) gene, leading to a premature stop codon.
source: DNA sequencing revealed that the causal mutation at the ein6-1 allele is a seven base pair (bp) deletion in the fifth exon of the RELATIVE OF EARLY FLOWERING6 (REF6, At3g48430) gene, leading to a premature stop codon (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA sequencing data and reference to a figure showing the mutation.

claim: REF6 encodes the major H3K27me3 demethylase in Arabidopsis.
source: REF6 encodes the major H3K27me3 demethylase in Arabidopsis (Lu et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lu et al., 2011.

claim: The een-1 mutation was discovered by Thermal Asymmetric Interlaced (TAIL)-PCR and also directly visualized using optical mapping of ultra-long Ler and ein6-1 een-1 DNA molecules.
source: The een-1 mutation was discovered by Thermal Asymmetric Interlaced (TAIL)-PCR and also directly visualized using optical mapping of ultra-long Ler and ein6-1 een-1 DNA molecules (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to figures showing TAIL-PCR and optical mapping results.

claim: een-1 arose from a genomic inversion event of a 83 kilobase pair (kb) region on chromosome four.
source: een-1 arose from a genomic inversion event of a 83 kilobase pair (kb) region on chromosome four.
evidence: The claim is supported by the genomic analysis described in the text and shown in figures.

claim: As a result of two fast neutron bombardment-induced double-strand breaks, one in the 5'UTR of EEN (At4g38495) and the other in the fourth intron of the AQUAPORIN INTERACTOR (AQI, At4g38220) gene, the entire EEN gene was fused with four exons of the AQI gene.
source: As a result of two fast neutron bombardment-induced double-strand breaks, one in the 5'UTR of EEN (At4g38495) and the other in the fourth intron of the AQUAPORIN INTERACTOR (AQI, At4g38220) gene, the entire EEN gene was fused with four exons of the AQI gene (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data and reference to figures showing the fusion event.

claim: Sequencing of the chimeric AQI-EEN genomic DNA and cDNA revealed that 14 bp of the EEN 5'UTR are now part of the AQI-EEN cDNA causing an open reading frame shift that results in a premature stop codon within the first exon of EEN.
source: Sequencing of the chimeric AQI-EEN genomic DNA and cDNA revealed that 14 bp of the EEN 5'UTR are now part of the AQI-EEN cDNA causing an open reading frame shift that results in a premature stop codon within the first exon of EEN (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequencing data and reference to figures showing the sequence details.

claim: EEN shares homology to yeast IES6, a crucial component of the yeast INO80 chromatin remodeling complex whose function is linked to eviction of the histone variant H2A.Z.
source: Interestingly, EEN shares homology to yeast IES6, a crucial component of the yeast INO80 chromatin remodeling complex whose function is linked to eviction of the histone variant H2A.Z (Papamichos-Chronakis et al., 2011; Chen et al., 2013) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on yeast IES6 and reference to a figure showing the homology.

claim: While both single mutants show nearly wild-type transcriptional responses to ET, ein6-1 een-1 double mutants are similar to ein2-45 mutants, being largely deficient in activating ET-dependent transcription.
source: While both single mutants show nearly wild-type transcriptional responses to ET, ein6-1 een-1 double mutants are similar to ein2-45 mutants, being largely deficient in activating ET-dependent transcription (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: While wild-type and single mutants accumulate similar levels of EIN3, ein6-1 een-1 mutants accumulate no EIN3 protein in response to ET treatment.
source: While wild-type and single mutants accumulate similar levels of EIN3, ein6-1 een-1 mutants accumulate no EIN3 protein in response to ET treatment (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Nuclear-localized EIN2C protein is absent in ein6-1 een-1 mutants.
source: However, nuclear-localized EIN2C protein is absent in ein6-1 een-1 mutants suggesting that the failure to accumulate EIN3 is due to the absence of EIN2C (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Results from RNA-seq indicate that the absence of nuclear-localized EIN2C can be explained by the reduction of EIN2 mRNA expression in ein6-1 een-1 double mutants.
source: Results from RNA-seq indicate that this absence can be explained by the reduction of EIN2 mRNA expression in ein6-1 een-1 double mutants (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: There were 2369 genes (Group I) that gain H3K27me3 in ein6-1 single mutants (2-fold enrichment over Ler) as well as in ein6-1 een-1 double mutants.
source: There were 2369 genes (Group I) that gain H3K27me3 in ein6-1 single mutants (2-fold enrichment over Ler) as well as in ein6-1 een-1 double mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: 54 additional genes (Group II) have significantly higher H3K27me3 levels (2-fold enrichment over ein6-1) in the double mutant.
source: We also found 54 additional genes (Group II) with significantly higher H3K27me3 levels (2-fold enrichment over ein6-1) in the double mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: EIN2 is in Group II and displays one of the strongest increases of H3K27me3 in ein6-1 een-1 mutants, with the mark spreading throughout the gene body.
source: Strikingly, EIN2 is in Group II and displays one of the strongest increases of H3K27me3 in ein6-1 een-1 mutants, with the mark spreading throughout the gene body (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 1E; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures and supplementary files.

claim: EIN6 (REF6) binds to the CTCTGYTY DNA motif at target genes through its C-terminal zinc fingers.
source: EIN6 (REF6) binds to the CTCTGYTY DNA motif at target genes through its C-terminal zinc fingers (Cui et al., 2016; Li et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on EIN6 (REF6) binding.

claim: The 5'UTR intron region of EIN2 contains two CTCTGYTY DNA motifs.
source: The 5'UTR intron region of EIN2 contains two of these DNA motifs (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to a figure showing the motif locations.

claim: Direct EIN6/EIN6-ZNF binding to EIN2 was observed within the 5'UTR intron and the gene body of EIN2.
source: We observed direct EIN6/EIN6-ZNF binding within the 5'UTR intron and the gene body of EIN2 (Figure 2C; Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq and DAP-seq data shown in figures.

claim: A truncated EIN6 (REF6) construct without the zinc fingers (EIN6ΔZNF) fails to complement the ein6-1 een-1 triple response phenotype.
source: The importance of the zinc fingers of EIN6 (REF6) for EIN2 regulation was further confirmed by the failure of a truncated EIN6 (REF6) construct without the zinc fingers (EIN6ΔZNF) to complement the ein6-1 een-1 triple response phenotype (Figure 2—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: The claim is supported by complementation assay data shown in a figure.

claim: EEN is a small YL1 nuclear protein C-terminal (YL1-C) domain-containing 14 kilodalton (kDa) protein that is cytoplasm- and nuclear-localized and expressed throughout the entire Arabidopsis seedling.
source: EEN is a small YL1 nuclear protein C-terminal (YL1-C) domain-containing 14 kilodalton (kDa) protein that is cytoplasm- and nuclear-localized and expressed throughout the entire Arabidopsis seedling (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by protein characterization data and reference to figures showing localization and expression.

claim: EEN binds to EIN2, especially in the 3'UTR region.
source: EEN also binds to EIN2, especially in the 3'UTR region (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures.

claim: The yeast homolog IES6 forms the nucleosome recognition module of the INO80 chromatin remodeling complex with ACTIN-RELATED PROTEIN5 (ARP5).
source: Its yeast homolog IES6 forms the nucleosome recognition module of the INO80 chromatin remodeling complex with ACTIN-RELATED PROTEIN5 (ARP5) (Eustermann et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a study on yeast IES6.

claim: This nucleosome recognition module is crucial for remodeling activity of the INO80 complex.
source: This module is crucial for remodeling activity of the INO80 complex (Tosi et al., 2013; Eustermann et al., 2018; Watanabe et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on the INO80 complex.

claim: In vitro pulldowns demonstrated an interaction between EEN and Arabidopsis ARP5.
source: In vitro pulldowns demonstrated an interaction between EEN and Arabidopsis ARP5 (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro pulldown data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Mass spectrometry (MS) analysis identified ARP5 as a strong EEN interactor.
source: To investigate whether this interaction also occurs in planta, mass spectrometry (MS) analysis was conducted which identified ARP5 as a strong EEN interactor (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D; Supplementary file 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in a figure and supplementary file.

claim: Compared to wild-type plants, 1866 genes were differentially expressed in ino80-8 mutants.
source: Compared to wild-type plants, 1866 genes were differentially expressed in ino80-8 mutants (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: These same genes were also differentially expressed in a remarkably similar manner in een-2 and arp5-1 mutants.
source: These same genes were also differentially expressed in a remarkably similar manner in een-2 and arp5-1 mutants (Figure 3C; Supplementary file 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C and supplementary file.

claim: Double mutants (ref6-1 een-2, ref6-1 ino80-1 and ref6-1 arp5-1) each strikingly display increased levels of H3K27me3 and H2A.Z at EIN2.
source: Finally, we generated double mutants (ref6-1 een-2, ref6-1 ino80-1 and ref6-1 arp5-1) that each strikingly display increased levels of H3K27me3 and H2A.Z at EIN2 (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I and J)
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures.

claim: These double mutants also exhibit a hypo-sensitive triple response phenotype, although not as severe as in ein6-1 een-1 mutants.
source: These double mutants also exhibit a hypo-sensitive triple response phenotype, although not as severe as in ein6-1 een-1 mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic data shown in a figure.

claim: ref6-1 een-2 pie1-1 triple mutants that are also deficient in the ATPase subunit of the SWR1 chromatin remodeling complex display a wild-type triple response phenotype.
source: Interestingly, ref6-1 een-2 pie1-1 triple mutants that are also deficient in the ATPase subunit of the SWR1 chromatin remodeling complex display a wild-type triple response phenotype (Noh and Amasino, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic data and a citation.

claim: The loss of chromatinized H2A.Z in pie1-1 mutants can suppress the hypo-sensitive triple response phenotype of ref6-1 een-2 mutants.
source: This result suggests that the loss of chromatinized H2A.Z in pie1-1 mutants can suppress the hypo-sensitive triple response phenotype of ref6-1 een-2 mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and H; Figure 3—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic data and reference to figures.

claim: A global defect of the H2A.Z landscape in ino80-1 mutants and mutants of INO80 complex subunits (een-1, een-2 and arp5-1) to wild-type was not observed.
source: Surprisingly, a global defect of the H2A.Z landscape in ino80-1 mutants and mutants of INO80 complex subunits (een-1, een-2 and arp5-1) to wild-type was not observed (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures.

claim: Except for pie1-1 mutants, the global impact on the H2A.Z landscape was only marginally affected in all tested single and double mutants.
source: Except for pie1-1 mutants, the global impact on the H2A.Z landscape was only marginally affected in all tested single and double mutants (Figure 4A and B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures.

claim: The gain of H2A.Z only becomes evident in double mutants at a few loci including EIN2.
source: Furthermore, the gain of H2A.Z only becomes evident in double mutants at a few loci including EIN2 (Figures 2A and 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures.

claim: EEN predominantly binds to gene bodies of environmentally responsive genes that harbor gene body H2A.Z.
source: Interestingly, ChIP-seq assays revealed that EEN predominantly binds to gene bodies of environmentally responsive genes that harbor gene body H2A.Z (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C; Supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures and supplementary file.

claim: Robust hormone-induced H2A.Z eviction (≥1.3 fold, air vs 4 hr ET) occurs at 1076 genes.
source: Thus, we examined the H2A.Z landscape in een-1 and ino80-8 mutants in ET-treated seedlings and found that robust hormone-induced H2A.Z eviction (≥1.3 fold, air vs 4 hr ET) occurs at 1076 genes (Supplementary file 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data and reference to a supplementary file.

claim: These eviction dynamics were compromised in een-1 and ino80-8 mutants suggesting that the Arabidopsis INO80 complex is involved in the H2A.Z eviction process.
source: These eviction dynamics were compromised in een-1 and ino80-8 mutants suggesting that the Arabidopsis INO80 complex is involved in the H2A.Z eviction process (Figure 4C and D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures.

claim: By using the broad H3K27me3 domain at EIN2 as a proxy for an aberrant chromatin signature in ein6-1 een-1 mutants, its presence was discovered in all tested ein6-1 een-1 tissues.
source: By using the broad H3K27me3 domain at EIN2 as a proxy for an aberrant chromatin signature in ein6-1 een-1 mutants, we discovered its presence in all tested ein6-1 een-1 tissues (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: These results indicate that EIN6 (REF6)/INO80-mediated control of EIN2 expression already occurs by early embryogenesis in wildtype and that its failure rapidly establishes a repressive chromatin state at EIN2.
source: These results indicate that EIN6 (REF6)/INO80-mediated control of EIN2 expression already occurs by early embryogenesis in wildtype and that its failure rapidly establishes a repressive chromatin state at EIN2.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the presence of the aberrant chromatin signature in all tested tissues including dry seeds.

claim: A key feature of the broad H3K27me3 domain at EIN2 in ein6-1 een-1 mutants is its asymmetric distribution across the gene with the peak level occurring within a 5'UTR intron and a steady decrease towards the 3'UTR.
source: A key feature of the broad H3K27me3 domain at EIN2 in ein6-1 een-1 mutants is its asymmetric distribution across the gene with the peak level occurring within a 5'UTR intron and a steady decrease towards the 3'UTR (Figures 2A and 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in figures.

claim: The 5'UTR intron is the region of EIN2 where the majority of H3K27me3, H2A.Z, H2Aub and H3K4me3 can be detected in wild-type plants.
source: The 5'UTR intron is also the region of EIN2 where the majority of H3K27me3, H2A.Z, H2Aub and H3K4me3 can be detected in wild-type plants (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Histochemical GUS staining revealed detectable reporter activity from the EIN2:GUS construct in wild-type but only minimal activity was observed in ein6-1 een-1 seedlings.
source: Histochemical GUS staining revealed detectable reporter activity from the EIN2:GUS construct in wild-type but only minimal activity was observed in ein6-1 een-1 seedlings (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GUS staining data shown in Figure 4B (note: the text refers to Figure 4B but this appears to be Figure 5B based on the content).

claim: Deletion of the 5'UTR intron resulted in strongly reduced GUS reporter activity in wild-type and ein6-1 een-1 EIN2ΔUI:GUS seedlings.
source: Deletion of the 5'UTR intron resulted in strongly reduced GUS reporter activity in wild-type and ein6-1 een-1 EIN2ΔUI:GUS seedlings (Figure 5B)
evidence: The claim is supported by GUS staining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The 5'UTR intron is necessary for EIN2 promoter-driven reporter activity.
source: Deletion of the 5'UTR intron resulted in strongly reduced GUS reporter activity in wild-type and ein6-1 een-1 EIN2ΔUI:GUS seedlings (Figure 5B), indicating that, not only is the 5'UTR intron necessary for EIN2 promoter-driven reporter activity
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the GUS reporter data.

claim: The loss of the 5'UTR intron phenocopies the ein6-1 een-1 mutant.
source: Deletion of the 5'UTR intron resulted in strongly reduced GUS reporter activity in wild-type and ein6-1 een-1 EIN2ΔUI:GUS seedlings (Figure 5B), indicating that, not only is the 5'UTR intron necessary for EIN2 promoter-driven reporter activity, but also that its loss phenocopies the ein6-1 een-1 mutant.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the GUS reporter data.

claim: The full length EIN2 5'UTR intron construct (UI1161:GUS) as well as two moderately 3'-truncated constructs (UI703:GUS and UI404:GUS) were able to drive GUS reporter activity to comparable levels.
source: We found that the full length EIN2 5'UTR intron construct (UI1161:GUS) as well as two moderately 3'-truncated constructs (UI703:GUS and UI404:GUS) were able to drive GUS reporter activity to comparable levels (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative GUS assay data shown in a figure.

claim: The most heavily 3'-truncated intron construct (UI170:GUS) had greater than six-fold higher GUS activity relative to the longer constructs, indicating the presence of an enhancer element in that region whose activity may be modulated by one or multiple regulatory elements further downstream in the 5'UTR intron region.
source: However, the most heavily 3'-truncated intron construct (UI170:GUS) had greater than six-fold higher GUS activity relative to the longer constructs, indicating the presence of an enhancer element in that region whose activity may be modulated by one or multiple regulatory elements further downstream in the 5'UTR intron region (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative GUS assay data and involves inference about the presence of regulatory elements.

claim: Similar GUS activities of UI1161:GUS, UI703:GUS and UI404:GUS suggest that regulatory elements are located within the +170 bp to +404 bp region and provide a landing platform for various, but yet unknown, transcriptional regulators.
source: Similar GUS activities of UI1161:GUS, UI703:GUS and UI404:GUS suggest that these regulatory elements are located within the +170 bp to +404 bp region and provide a landing platform for various, but yet unknown, transcriptional regulators.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the GUS activity data.

claim: bHLH122 and SQUAMOSA PROMOTER BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 5 (SPL5) were identified as potential candidate transcription factors that can bind to the 5'UTR region of EIN2.
source: By interrogating the Plant Cistrome Database (O'Malley et al., 2016), we identified bHLH122 and SQUAMOSA PROMOTER BINDING PROTEIN-LIKE 5 (SPL5) as potential candidate transcription factors (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from the Plant Cistrome Database.

claim: SPL15 associates with the MADS-box protein SOC1 which in turn recruits EIN6 (REF6) to remodel the chromatin environment at SPL15/SOC1 target genes.
source: It is known from SPL15 that it associates with the MADS-box protein SOC1 which in turn recruits EIN6 (REF6) to remodel the chromatin environment at SPL15/SOC1 target genes (Hyun et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hyun et al., 2016.

claim: The ein6-1 mutants carry mutations in two genes that encode the H3K27me3 demethylase REF6 (EIN6) as well as a crucial subunit of the INO80 chromatin remodeling complex (EEN).
source: Here we unravel a novel regulatory mechanism at EIN2, a multifunctional component of a critical stress regulatory pathway in plants. We discovered that the ein6-1 mutants carry mutations in two genes that encode the H3K27me3 demethylase REF6 (EIN6) as well as a crucial subunit of the INO80 chromatin remodeling complex (EEN).
evidence: The claim is supported by the genetic and molecular characterization described in the manuscript.

claim: Only the presence of both mutations led to the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 and H2A.Z at EIN2.
source: Remarkably only the presence of both mutations led to the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 and H2A.Z at EIN2.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data showing differential accumulation in single versus double mutants.

claim: The resulting repressive chromatin state compromises EIN2 mRNA expression leading to a strongly reduced ET-induced accumulation of EIN3 protein and ultimately to a failure of the transcriptional response.
source: The resulting repressive chromatin state compromises EIN2 mRNA expression leading to a strongly reduced ET-induced accumulation of EIN3 protein and ultimately to a failure of the transcriptional response.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq, Western blot, and phenotypic data.

claim: H3K27me3 and H2A.Z strongly co-associate in Arabidopsis.
source: H3K27me3 and H2A.Z strongly co-associate in Arabidopsis which is not surprising since the majority of Arabidopsis genes are marked with H2A.Z (Dong et al., 2012; Carter et al., 2018; Gómez-Zambrano et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on H3K27me3 and H2A.Z.

claim: The majority of Arabidopsis genes are marked with H2A.Z.
source: H3K27me3 and H2A.Z strongly co-associate in Arabidopsis which is not surprising since the majority of Arabidopsis genes are marked with H2A.Z (Dong et al., 2012; Carter et al., 2018; Gómez-Zambrano et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on H2A.Z.

claim: H3K27me3 and H2A.Z mutually reinforce their deposition through the concerted action of the methyltransferase CURLY LEAF (CLF) and the ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler PIE1 and PICKLE (PKL).
source: Interestingly, they mutually reinforce their deposition through the concerted action of the methyltransferase CURLY LEAF (CLF) and the ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler PIE1 and PICKLE (PKL) (Carter et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Carter et al., 2018.

claim: PIE1-dependent H2A.Z incorporation promotes the deposition of H3K27me3 which is retained after DNA replication by PKL.
source: PIE1-dependent H2A.Z incorporation promotes the deposition of H3K27me3 which is retained after DNA replication by PKL (Carter et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Carter et al., 2018.

claim: Non-evicted H2A.Z at EIN2 initially leads to increased deposition of H3K27me3.
source: This scenario of a mutual reinforcement can explain the accumulation of H3K27me3 and H2A.Z in the ein6-1 een-1 double mutant background. It's possible that non-evicted H2A.Z at EIN2 initially leads to increased deposition of H3K27me3.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the mutual reinforcement mechanism.

claim: Since H3K27me3 demethylation and H2A.Z eviction are both functionally impaired in ein6-1 een-1 mutants, H3K27me3 and H2A.Z can continuously reinforce their deposition, which ultimately leads to the observed gene body-wide spreading of both marks at EIN2.
source: Since H3K27me3 demethylation and H2A.Z eviction are both functionally impaired in ein6-1 een-1 mutants, H3K27me3 and H2A.Z can continuously reinforce their deposition, which ultimately leads to the observed gene body-wide spreading of both marks at EIN2.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the functional impairments and observed data.

claim: Monoubiquitination of H2A.Z confers H2A.Z-mediated transcriptional repression.
source: Another interesting aspect arose from a recent study showing that monoubiquitination of H2A.Z confers H2A.Z-mediated transcriptional repression (Gómez-Zambrano et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gómez-Zambrano et al., 2019.

claim: The observed increase of H2Aub at the gene body of EIN2 in ein6-1 een-1 mutants is predominantly monoubiquitinated H2A.Z.
source: Although our anti-H2Aub antibody cannot distinguish between monoubiquitinated H2A and monoubiquitinated H2A.Z, we speculate that the observed increase of H2Aub at the gene body of EIN2 in ein6-1 een-1 mutants is predominantly monoubiquitinated H2A.Z.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the H2A.Z accumulation data.

claim: Although the functional loss of EIN6 (REF6) as the major Arabidopsis H3K27me3 demethylase has a profound impact on the H3K27me3 landscape in Arabidopsis, EIN2 is only marginally affected.
source: However, it's unclear why the increased mutually enforced deposition of H3K27me3 and H2A.Z can only be observed in the double mutant background. Although the functional loss of EIN6 (REF6) as the major Arabidopsis H3K27me3 demethylase has a profound impact on the H3K27me3 landscape in Arabidopsis (Lu et al., 2011), EIN2 is only marginally affected.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data and a citation.

claim: A molecular hallmark of ein6 (ref6) mutants is the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 at thousands of genes (2369 Group I genes).
source: A molecular hallmark of ein6 (ref6) mutants is the ectopic accumulation of H3K27me3 at thousands of genes (2369 Group I genes) (Lu et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data and a citation.

claim: The in-depth investigation of the ein6-1 een-1 epigenome revealed a new class of genes (Group II genes), such as EIN2, that ectopically accumulates H3K27me3 in the ein6-1 (ref6-1) mutant background but only when INO80 is simultaneously lost (ref6-1 ino80-1) or the INO80 complex activity is simultaneously impaired (ein6-1 een-1, ref6-1 een-2, ref6-1 arp5-1).
source: Our in-depth investigation of the ein6-1 een-1 epigenome revealed a new class of genes (Group II genes), such as EIN2, that ectopically accumulates H3K27me3 in the ein6-1 (ref6-1) mutant background but only when INO80 is simultaneously lost (ref6-1 ino80-1) or the INO80 complex activity is simultaneously impaired (ein6-1 een-1, ref6-1 een-2, ref6-1 arp5-1).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data from multiple mutant combinations.

claim: These findings indicate an EIN6 (REF6)-independent INO80-mediated mechanism that specifically prevents H3K27me3 hyper-accumulation at EIN2 in the absence of EIN6.
source: These findings indicate an EIN6 (REF6)-independent INO80-mediated mechanism that specifically prevents H3K27me3 hyper-accumulation at EIN2 in the absence of EIN6.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the genetic and ChIP-seq data.

claim: The mouse H3K27me3 demethylases Jmjd3 and UTX interact with T-box transcription factors and a Brg1-containing SWI/SNF remodeling complex to activate gene expression in a H3K27me3 demethylase-independent manner.
source: The mouse H3K27me3 demethylases Jmjd3 and UTX interact with T-box transcription factors and a Brg1-containing SWI/SNF remodeling complex to activate gene expression in a H3K27me3 demethylase-independent manner (Miller et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Miller et al., 2010.

claim: In Arabidopsis, EIN6 (REF6) physically interacts with BRAHMA (BRM) and is crucially involved in recruiting BRM to its target genes.
source: In Arabidopsis, EIN6 (REF6) physically interacts with BRAHMA (BRM) and is crucially involved in recruiting BRM to its target genes (Li et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2016.

claim: In contrast to ein6-1 een-1 double mutants, brm-1 ref6-1 double mutants show no additional ectopic H3K27me3 domains.
source: However, in contrast to ein6-1 een-1 double mutants, brm-1 ref6-1 double mutants show no additional ectopic H3K27me3 domains (Li et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2016.

claim: The most prominent function of the INO80 chromatin remodeling complex is the eviction of the histone variant H2A.Z.
source: The most prominent function of the INO80 chromatin remodeling complex is the eviction of the histone variant H2A.Z (Papamichos-Chronakis et al., 2011; Alatwi and Downs, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on the INO80 complex.

claim: In the absence of a stimulus or an ein6 (ref6) background mutation, single mutants of the Arabidopsis INO80 complex (een-1, een-2, arp5-1, ino80-1, ino80-8) have no impact on global H2A.Z occupancy which in line with a recent report in yeast.
source: However, in the absence of a stimulus or an ein6 (ref6) background mutation, single mutants of the Arabidopsis INO80 complex (een-1, een-2, arp5-1, ino80-1, ino80-8) have no impact on global H2A.Z occupancy which in line with a recent report in yeast (Jeronimo et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data and a citation.

claim: There is an INO80-independent H2A.Z removal mechanism in Arabidopsis, like in mammals.
source: This strongly suggests that, like in mammals, there is an INO80-independent H2A.Z removal mechanism in Arabidopsis (Obri et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the data and a citation to a mammalian study.

claim: The INO80 complex is crucial for pluripotency of embryonic stem cells (ESCs).
source: The INO80 complex is crucial for pluripotency of embryonic stem cells (ESCs) (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2014.

claim: Silencing of INO80 leads to a breakdown of the ESC-specific chromatin structure that is accompanied by the accumulation of H3K27me3 at INO80 target sites.
source: Silencing of INO80 leads to a breakdown of the ESC-specific chromatin structure that is accompanied by the accumulation of H3K27me3 at INO80 target sites (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2014.

claim: It is conceivable that the INO80 complex can prevent H3K27me3 accumulation by antagonizing PRC2-mediated H3K27me3 deposition through direct or indirect blocking of the access of PRC2 to chromatin.
source: Based on this and our findings, it is conceivable that the INO80 complex can prevent H3K27me3 accumulation by antagonizing PRC2-mediated H3K27me3 deposition through direct or indirect blocking of the access of PRC2 to chromatin.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on findings from ESCs and the current study.

claim: Loss of EIN6 (REF6) has no effect on the global H2A.Z distribution, but leads to an ectopic H2A.Z accumulation at EIN2 in the een mutant.
source: Loss of EIN6 (REF6) also has no effect on the global H2A.Z distribution, but leads to an ectopic H2A.Z accumulation at EIN2 in the een mutant.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data.

claim: EIN6 can control chromatin structure through H3K27me3 demethylation and through the regulation of H2A.Z occupancy, although in a very specific genomic context.
source: This suggests that EIN6 can not only control chromatin structure through H3K27me3 demethylation, but also through the regulation of H2A.Z occupancy, although in a very specific genomic context.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the ChIP-seq data.

claim: The hypo-sensitive triple response phenotype of ref6-1 een-2 mutants can be suppressed by the loss of SWR1-deposited H2A.Z in ref6-1 een-2 pie1-1 triple mutants.
source: This is supported by our finding that the hypo-sensitive triple response phenotype of ref6-1 een-2 mutants can be suppressed by the loss of SWR1-deposited H2A.Z in ref6-1 een-2 pie1-1 triple mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic data.

claim: EIN6 (REF6) might control H2A.Z occupancy through blocking SWR1-mediated deposition of H2A.Z.
source: Similar to the INO80-mediated restriction of PRC2 chromatin access, EIN6 (REF6) might control H2A.Z occupancy through blocking SWR1-mediated deposition of H2A.Z.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the genetic data.

claim: The observed functional duality of EIN6 (REF6) and the INO80 complex in antagonizing SWR1-mediated H2A.Z incorporation and PRC2-mediated H3K27 tri-methylation represents a double safeguard mechanism that ensures a permissive chromatin structure at EIN2 to ultimately safeguard its expression.
source: We speculate that the observed functional duality of EIN6 (REF6) and the INO80 complex in antagonizing SWR1-mediated H2A.Z incorporation and PRC2-mediated H3K27 tri-methylation represents a double safeguard mechanism that ensures a permissive chromatin structure at EIN2 to ultimately safeguard its expression (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on all the data presented.

claim: Since EIN2 is not the only gene that is directly targeted by EIN6 and EEN, other specificity determinants must exist.
source: The question of why a gene like EIN2 is controlled by this pivotal chromatin modifier equilibrium is not fully answered. Since EIN2 is not the only gene that is directly targeted by EIN6 and EEN, other specificity determinants must exist.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the ChIP-seq data showing multiple targets.

claim: The majority of chromatin regulation at EIN2 takes place in the 5'UTR intron region.
source: The majority of chromatin regulation at EIN2 takes place in the 5'UTR intron region and our functional analysis of this region indicates the presence of multiple regulatory elements.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq and functional analysis data.

claim: There is likely a yet unknown transcription factor that is required to establish the EIN6/INO80-dependent double safeguard mechanism at EIN2.
source: Thus, we believe there is likely a yet unknown transcription factor that is required to establish the EIN6/INO80-dependent double safeguard mechanism at EIN2 (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the functional analysis of the 5'UTR intron.

claim: It is plausible that the EIN6/INO80-mediated double safeguard is actively turned off to allow stable repression of EIN2 in a specific cell type and/or at a specific developmental stage.
source: Besides safeguarding EIN2 expression, it's also plausible that the EIN6/INO80-mediated double safeguard is actively turned off to allow stable repression of EIN2 in a specific cell type and/or at a specific developmental stage.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about potential regulatory scenarios.

claim: Histone signatures are mitotically stable and potentially echo prior or missing regulatory steps.
source: Histone signatures are mitotically stable and potentially echo prior or missing regulatory steps (Wang and Higgins, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang and Higgins, 2013.

claim: With the finding that dry ein6-1 een-1 seeds already display the aberrant chromatin signature at EIN2, it can be envisioned that the EIN6/INO80-mediated regulation already takes place during embryogenesis.
source: In addition, with our finding that dry ein6-1 een-1 seeds already display the aberrant chromatin signature at EIN2, it can be envisioned that the EIN6/INO80-mediated regulation already takes place during embryogenesis.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the ChIP-seq data from dry seeds.

claim: The relatively weak binding of EIN6 and EEN to EIN2 might be explained by the number of cells with EIN6/EEN-binding at EIN2 being rather small or that DNA residency times and chromatin remodeler compositions may vary between genes.
source: This might also provide an explanation for the relatively weak binding of EIN6 and EEN to EIN2. Since we were able to capture strong EIN6 and EEN binding at numerous loci, technical reasons for weak binding such as insufficient crosslinking to the DNA are less likely. It is also plausible that the number of cells with EIN6/EEN-binding at EIN2 is rather small or that DNA residency times and chromatin remodeler compositions may vary between genes, thus potentially affecting the outcome of our ChIP-seq experiments.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the ChIP-seq results.

claim: This newly discovered mode of regulation at EIN2, not only fine-tunes its expression, but may also provide an efficient switch to repress gene expression.
source: Given EIN2's multifunctional role in controlling many agronomically important processes (Johnson and Ecker, 1998), we propose that this newly discovered mode of regulation at EIN2, not only fine-tunes its expression, but may also provide an efficient switch to repress gene expression.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about the functional significance of the findings, supported by a citation.

claim: The gaseous plant hormone ethylene regulates numerous biological processes ranging from development to responses to environmental stimuli.
source: The gaseous plant hormone ethylene regulates numerous biological processes ranging from development to responses to environmental stimuli (Johnson and Ecker, 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Johnson and Ecker, 1998.

claim: The ET signaling pathway evolved over 450 million years ago with EIN2 as its master regulator.
source: The ET signaling pathway evolved over 450 million years ago with EIN2 as its master regulator (Alonso et al., 1999; Ju et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on the ET signaling pathway.

claim: In the absence of ethylene, EIN2 is constitutively phosphorylated by the Raf-like protein kinase CONSTITUTIVE TRIPLE RESPONSE1 (CTR1).
source: In the absence of ethylene, EIN2 is constitutively phosphorylated by the Raf-like protein kinase CONSTITUTIVE TRIPLE RESPONSE1 (CTR1).
evidence: The claim is established knowledge about the ET signaling pathway.

claim: Upon ET perception, EIN2 is no longer phosphorylated by CTR1, resulting in the proteolytic cleavage of EIN2's C-terminal CEND domain (EIN2C).
source: Upon ET perception, EIN2 is no longer phosphorylated by CTR1, resulting in the proteolytic cleavage of EIN2's C-terminal CEND domain (EIN2C) (Ju et al., 2012; Qiao et al., 2012; Wen et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on EIN2 processing.

claim: In the cytoplasm, EIN2C functions to facilitate the translational repression of mRNAs for the EIN3/EIL1-degrading F-box proteins EIN3 BINDING F BOX1/2 (EBF1/EBF2) in cytoplasmic P-bodies.
source: In the cytoplasm, EIN2C functions to facilitate the translational repression of mRNAs for the EIN3/EIL1-degrading F-box proteins EIN3 BINDING F BOX1/2 (EBF1/EBF2) in cytoplasmic P-bodies (Merchante et al., 2015; Li et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on EIN2C function.

claim: EIN2C translocates to the nucleus where it stabilizes the ethylene response master regulatory transcription factors (TFs) EIN3 and EIL1 through a currently unknown mechanism.
source: EIN2C also translocates to the nucleus where it stabilizes the ethylene response master regulatory transcription factors (TFs) EIN3 and EIL1 through a currently unknown mechanism (Ju et al., 2012; Qiao et al., 2012; Wen et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on EIN2C function.

claim: Nuclear-localized EIN2C also directly regulates histone acetylation through an association with EIN2 NUCLEAR-ASSOCIATED PROTEIN1 (ENAP1) at ET-responsive genes.
source: In addition, nuclear-localized EIN2C also directly regulates histone acetylation through an association with EIN2 NUCLEAR-ASSOCIATED PROTEIN1 (ENAP1) at ET-responsive genes (Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2017.

claim: ET is crucial for the integration of biotic and abiotic stress responses into plant growth pathways.
source: ET is crucial for the integration of biotic and abiotic stress responses into plant growth pathways (Dubois et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dubois et al., 2018.

claim: ein2 loss-of-function alleles display severe stress-related phenotypes in Arabidopsis as well as in many other species including the legume Medicago truncatula and rice (Oryza sativa).
source: which is underscored by the severe stress-related phenotypes displayed by ein2 loss-of-function alleles in Arabidopsis (Alonso et al., 1999) as well as in many other species including the legume Medicago truncatula and rice (Oryza sativa) (Penmetsa et al., 2008; Ma et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies on ein2 mutants.

claim: Despite EIN2's importance for fitness under adverse growth conditions across land plants, its transcriptional regulation and underlying chromatin architecture are completely uncharacterized.
source: Yet despite EIN2's importance for fitness under adverse growth conditions across land plants, its transcriptional regulation and underlying chromatin architecture are completely uncharacterized.
evidence: The claim is a statement about the state of knowledge prior to this study.

claim: Through the molecular characterization of the ET-insensitive ein6-1 mutant, it was discovered that the major Arabidopsis H3K27me3 demethylase RELATIVE OF EARLY FLOWERING6 (REF6) and the INO80 chromatin remodeling complex cooperatively regulate H3K27me3 and H2A.Z occupancy in the 5'UTR intron of EIN2.
source: Here we combined genomics, genetics and biochemistry to explore the chromatin environment at EIN2. Through the molecular characterization of the ET-insensitive ein6-1 mutant, we discovered that the major Arabidopsis H3K27me3 demethylase RELATIVE OF EARLY FLOWERING6 (REF6) (Lu et al., 2011) and the INO80 chromatin remodeling complex cooperatively regulate H3K27me3 and H2A.Z occupancy in the 5'UTR intron of EIN2.
evidence: The claim is supported by the combined genomics, genetics and biochemistry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In addition to their prominent functions (H3K27me3 demethylation and H2A.Z eviction), EIN6 (REF6) and the INO80 complex also antagonize SWR1-mediated H2A.Z incorporation and PRC2-mediated tri-methylation of H3K27, respectively.
source: Importantly, we also propose that in addition to their prominent functions (H3K27me3 demethylation and H2A.Z eviction), EIN6 (REF6) and the INO80 complex also antagonize SWR1-mediated H2A.Z incorporation and PRC2-mediated tri-methylation of H3K27, respectively.
evidence: The claim is a proposal based on the data presented, involving speculation about additional functions.

claim: Concomitant loss of EIN6 (REF6) and the INO80 complex shifts the chromatin landscape at EIN2 to a repressive state causing a dramatic reduction of EIN2 expression.
source: Concomitant loss of EIN6 (REF6) and the INO80 complex shifts the chromatin landscape at EIN2 to a repressive state causing a dramatic reduction of EIN2 expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: These results uncover a unique type of chromatin regulation which safeguards the expression of an essential multifunctional plant stress regulator.
source: These results uncover a unique type of chromatin regulation which safeguards the expression of an essential multifunctional plant stress regulator.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement about the significance of the findings.
